summary.headline: Senco Gold Q4 FY26 revenue up 45% YoY to INR1,997 crore, but management guides FY27 growth of only 18-20% and a 7.5-7.8% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,997 crore (up 45% YoY), EBITDA INR274 crore (up 116%) and PAT INR157 crore (up 151%), with reported EBITDA margin of 13.7%. FY26 sales reached INR8,430 crore (about 33% growth), with gains driven by gold price rises, new stores and old gold exchange. Management said the 13.7% Q4 and 11.5% full-year margins include a customs-duty inventory gain and gold price effects, and that sustainable EBITDA is 7.5-7.8%. Post the PM's appeal in late May, footfalls fell for 7-10 days and May was broadly flat YoY, and the call left the inventory build (188 days) and negative free cash flow as the main open questions.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin (gross, as reported)

segments.name: Jewellery
segments.commentary: Coins and bullion were about 6% of FY26 sales, with the balance entirely jewellery. Diamond jewellery value grew 32% YoY and volume grew 9%; stud ratio is about 11%.

segments.name: Sennes (lab-grown diamonds and lifestyle)
segments.commentary: Operates 12 exclusive stores; management says the business is EBITDA positive at the total brand level in its second year. Management plans to invest INR50-100 crore in the brand.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20% (CEO also cited 20-25% in the Q&A; CFO framed it as a conservative floor with an internal target higher), implying about INR10,000-10,500 crore.
Sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 7.5-7.8%; management says FY26 gross margin benefited 2.5-3% from gold price rise and sees only 10-15 bps of YoY margin improvement from operating leverage.
PAT margin guided at 4.0-4.5%; CEO said FY25-26 margins were 3.5-4% in general, and FY26 is higher due to inventory gains.
18-20 new stores in FY27, franchise-led; pipeline skewed to Bihar and UP.
Inventory days target of 160-180 (CFO) / 150-160 benchmark (CEO); the 188-day level is seen as the peak.
Sustainable ROE/ROCE of about 15.5-16% for the full year, with 17%+ targeted over 2-3 years excluding inventory gains.
Marketing spend guided at 1.8-2.2% of revenue; GML (gold metal loan) to be raised back to 50%+ from current lower level, at a 3-3.5% borrowing cost.

Customs duty inventory gain estimated at about 9% of ~INR4,500 crore gold inventory; CFO said effective gain at least 6-7%, recognised over Q1-Q2 FY27 as inventory reprices daily from 30 June to 30 September.
capex_capacity: Opened 7 new own showrooms in Q4 FY26 and 26 in FY26; plans 18-20 stores in FY27, mainly franchise-led.
New markets: Rajasthan (Bikaner, franchise), Central Maharashtra (Nagpur), Western UP, and Madhya Pradesh (franchisee); Bihar and UP form the FY27 pipeline.

Own factory manufacturing is 4-5% of gold jewellery; target 10% (about 8-9% of total manufacturing in value terms by the CFO's calculation). About 70-75% is through karigars and 20% ready-made purchases.
Hedging is about 40-50% of inventory, with policy up to 80%; MCX margins are now about 25-26%, which limits hedging capacity.
demand_pricing: Akshaya Tritiya/Poila Boishakh (April 2026) growth about 66-67% YoY; West Bengal +69%, East Bengal +78%, North Bengal +75%, Northeast +64%, Central +162%; April primary sales about INR1,500 crore.
May 2026 after the PM's appeal: footfalls down for 7-10 days; management says May YTD is broadly in line with last May. Adhik Maas and heat wave cited as reasons.

Average ticket value up about 30% YoY; lightweight design portfolio is over 1.5 lakh designs; 9-carat and 14-carat ranges are gaining traction; 9-carat and 14-carat are about 13-15% of sales (15-20% for gold per CEO).
Old gold exchange was about 44% of FY26 revenue and about 50% in Q4 FY26; management sees 50-55% as the benchmark, with no direct margin impact; no melting loss charged currently (0.1-0.2% risk).
Competition: organised players from South and West entering West Bengal and other markets; local unorganised players discounting (e.g., Delhi), which limits margin expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the guided mix of old gold exchange going forward and its margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees a 50-55% old gold exchange share as the monitored range and no direct margin impact, citing history of 25-30% to 35-40% to about 50% without margin pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory gain from the customs duty hike and how will it be recognised?
qa_highlights.answer: Gain is recognised as inventory is sold, likely across two quarters; CFO estimated effective gain at least 6-7% on ~INR4,500 crore gold inventory, reprices daily from 30 June to 30 September.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 20% growth when the first months are much higher?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said guidance is conservative; FY25 guidance of 20-25% was exceeded at 35%; volumes will fall due to higher gold prices while value grows 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Why no operating leverage at higher revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said competition (organised and unorganised, including discounting) limits margin gain to 10-15 bps at most; CEO said balance is needed between acquiring customers and profitability.

qa_highlights.question: How does 9-carat and lower-purity jewellery feature, and is it promoted?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said 9-carat and 14-carat account for 15-20% of gold and about 13-15% overall; company is advertising 9-carat through campaigns and says more awareness is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the margin gap versus Titan?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO attributed most of the gap to Titan's higher diamond-studded jewellery share and said Senco is working to grow diamond sales and lightweight designs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did GML fall and what is the borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: GML fell because of a cash flow mismatch in March when gold rose to about INR1,80,000 per 10g and positions were squared off; GML is at 3-3.5% cost, and the company aims for 50%+. ClearEdge upgraded rating by one notch; ICRA renewal pending.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable ROE/ROCE and FCF outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said ROE/ROCE of about 15.5-16%, and north of 16-17% over time, excluding inventory gains; management declined to guide positive free cash flow in the next 1-2 years.

risks_watch: Inventory days at 186-188 (up from ~166) and inventory value up 61% to INR5,296 crore; gains reverse if gold prices fall or duty changes again (duty cut from 15% to 5-6% next year).
Hedging capacity: MCX margins about 25-26% and GML duty exposure at 15% leave part of inventory unhedged; management promised more detail in Q1.
Near-term demand softness: footfalls fell after the PM's appeal and Adhik Maas; FY27 guidance of 18-20% growth implies low single-digit growth in the rest of FY27 per an analyst's arithmetic.
Margin pressure from competition and discounting in West Bengal and other markets; management guides margin gains of only 10-15 bps.
Negative free cash flow with no near-term guidance; increased borrowing costs in Q4 and possibly Q1 FY27 from lower GML share.
Advance gold to manufacturers has started in the last 1-2 months; the share is not disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year record and long-term targets, but cautious on near-term demand after the late-May slowdown; management repeatedly described guidance as conservative. It was evasive on quantifying inventory gains, free cash flow and the advance-gold share, and on the Sennes and gold-volume questions.
key_quotes: There are possibilities of increasing it further, maybe from 50% to 55%.
So, we are not charging any kind of melting losses or the whole cost of procuring the old gold from the customer for exchange purposes.
So, it is a lot of balancing that we need to do and ultimately work towards the 150 to 160 days inventory.
So, I think that the momentum of old gold is only going to increase, along with the 9-carat and lightweight jewellery.

adds.what: 18-20 new stores in FY27, mainly franchise-led (Bihar and UP pipeline)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20% (CEO cited 20-25% in Q&A), backed by 18-20 planned mainly franchise stores in Bihar/UP and new markets, but no order book or hard capacity numbers; Q4 FY26 revenue +45% YoY, though May was flat YoY after a post-PM-appeal footfall dip.
